home-remodeling.h1: Coral Gables homes, remade with respect
home-remodeling.hero_sub: Whole-home remodels for Merrick-era Mediterraneans and waterfront estates alike — permitted through Coral Gables Development Services, supervised daily, and built by a licensed South Florida general contractor, Lic. CGC1539072.
intro_paragraphs: Coral Gables was drawn by George Merrick in the 1920s, and much of it still looks the part: Mediterranean Revival homes with barrel tile roofs and arched loggias in the Country Club Section and Riviera, coral rock cottages near the Granada Golf Course, and waterfront estates in Cocoplum and Gables Estates. What owners of these homes actually want is rarely a teardown. It is the original architecture wrapped around a modern interior, with open sightlines, real closets, new mechanicals, and impact glass. A serious home remodeling project here keeps the character and quietly replaces everything behind it.

Remodeling here runs through the City of Coral Gables Development Services Department, and anything that touches the exterior, from windows and doors to paint colors, goes to the Board of Architects before the Building Division reviews it. Designated historic homes add a Certificate of Appropriateness through the city's preservation staff or board. Impact windows and doors need Miami-Dade product approvals for the High-Velocity Hurricane Zone, and if the project involves site work, the city's tree protections apply. None of this is a reason to panic. It is a reason to hire a contractor who has been through it before.

PGX Builders Group has spent 20-plus years building in South Florida, with more than 150 remodels and additions delivered, every one permitted and inspected. In Coral Gables we work the way the neighborhoods expect: a fixed written scope before demolition starts, a supervisor on site daily, floors and finishes protected, and crews who understand that a guard gate in Cocoplum is not a suggestion. One team carries your project from estimate to final inspection to warranty, so there is exactly one phone number to call when you have a question.
home-remodeling.scope_intro: Every Coral Gables remodel is scoped in writing before we open a wall. These are the pieces we most often put together for Merrick-era homes and newer estates.

scope_items.name: Opening up the formal rooms
scope_items.desc: Removing walls between formal rooms, adding steel or engineered lumber where 1920s masonry needs help, and getting the calculations sealed and permitted.

scope_items.name: New panels, pipes, and ducts
scope_items.desc: New electrical service and panels, modern supply lines and drains, and quiet high-efficiency HVAC replacing systems that predate air conditioning itself.

scope_items.name: Impact glass for Mediterranean facades
scope_items.desc: Miami-Dade approved impact glazing in profiles the Board of Architects will accept, because hurricane protection should not flatten a Mediterranean facade.

scope_items.name: Trim and doors, properly scaled
scope_items.desc: Custom cabinetry, restored or replicated interior doors, and baseboards and casings scaled to older ceilings instead of off-the-shelf trim that looks lost.

scope_items.name: Kitchens and baths, integrated
scope_items.desc: Both trades sequenced inside the larger remodel so plumbing, waterproofing, and stone work happen once, in the right order, under one permit set.

faqs.q: Do I need Board of Architects approval to remodel my Coral Gables home?
faqs.a: Only if the work shows from outside. Interior remodels go through the Building Division without a Board of Architects hearing. The moment your scope touches windows, doors, exterior colors, or the roofline, the Board reviews it first, and its approval is required before the building permit advances. We prepare submittals with that sequence in mind, so the review happens once instead of three times.

faqs.q: My house is a designated historic landmark. Can I still remodel it?
faqs.a: Yes, and plenty of Gables owners have. Exterior changes to a designated property need a Certificate of Appropriateness from the city's historic preservation staff or board before permits are issued, and minor in-kind work can often be approved administratively. Interiors are generally yours to reimagine. The practical effect is a longer runway, not a locked door, and we build that runway into the schedule from day one.

faqs.q: How long does a whole-home remodel take in Coral Gables?
faqs.a: Longer than a bathroom, shorter than you fear, and honestly dependent on approvals. Interior-only scopes can move quickly once permitted. Projects involving Board of Architects review, historic approvals, or structural engineering typically spend a few months in design and permitting before construction, and construction itself commonly runs several months to a year for a full house. We give you a written schedule with the estimate and then supervise daily to defend it.

faqs.q: What does a whole-home remodel cost in Coral Gables?
faqs.a: There is no honest one-number answer, because a cosmetic refresh and a full gut with new mechanicals are different animals. What we can promise is a fixed written scope with real allowances instead of a teaser number that grows through change orders. PGX is a high-end contractor: we are rarely the lowest bid, and our clients hire us so the number they sign is the number they pay, barring genuine surprises we document in writing.

faqs.q: Can we live in the house during a remodel?
faqs.a: Sometimes, and we will tell you plainly when the answer should be no. Phased work can keep a wing livable if the scope allows, with dust barriers, protected pathways, and mechanical continuity. Full-gut projects with open ceilings and no working kitchen are miserable to camp inside, so most Gables clients relocate for the heavy phase and return early for finishes. We plan the sequencing either way before demolition starts.

home-remodeling.cta_sub: Bring the wish list and the floor plan if you have one. You will get straight answers and a written estimate, in English o en español.

kitchen-remodeling.title: Custom Kitchen Remodeling, Coral Gables FL | PGX Builders
kitchen-remodeling.meta_description: Custom kitchen remodeling for Coral Gables homes — cabinetry, stone, structural openings, permits handled. Licensed GC. Call PGX at (786) 273-2524.
kitchen-remodeling.h1: Kitchens worthy of a Gables address
kitchen-remodeling.hero_sub: Custom cabinetry, stone counters, and structural openings for Coral Gables kitchens — designed around how you cook, permitted through the city, and supervised daily by a licensed general contractor.
kitchen-remodeling.local_heading: The kitchen your 1926 floor plan never imagined
intro_paragraphs: The classic Coral Gables kitchen problem is architectural. Merrick-era homes in Riviera, the Country Club Section, and the French Village were designed when kitchens were service rooms, tucked behind the dining room and sized for one cook who was not the homeowner. Today the kitchen is where everyone stands. So the high-end kitchen remodeling project here is usually a rescue mission: absorbing a butler's pantry or breakfast room, opening a masonry wall to the dining room, and putting a proper island where a bank of 1950s cabinets used to be.

An interior-only kitchen remodel in Coral Gables goes to the city's Development Services Department for permits and plan review without a stop at the Board of Architects. Change anything visible from outside, such as enlarging the window over the sink, venting through the facade, or cutting a new door to the terrace, and Board review comes first. Kitchens in designated historic homes may also need a Certificate of Appropriateness for exterior changes. Then there is the unglamorous part: plenty of older Gables houses need electrical service upgrades before they can run a modern appliance package, and we fold that work into the same permit.

PGX builds kitchens the way cabinetmakers wish contractors would: measured twice, sequenced properly, stone templated after the cabinets are set rather than before. You get a fixed written scope, a supervisor on site every day, and dust protection that treats the rest of your house as the finished product it is. Over 20-plus years in South Florida we have delivered more than 150 remodels and additions, all permitted and inspected, and a Gables kitchen gets nothing looser than that standard.
kitchen-remodeling.scope_heading: What we build into a Gables kitchen
kitchen-remodeling.scope_intro: Every kitchen is scoped line by line before demolition starts. These are the elements that come up most often in Gables homes.

scope_items.name: Cabinetry, not catalog sizes
scope_items.desc: Built-to-order cabinet packages with proper face frames or European boxes, finished to survive Miami humidity, and sized to older ceilings rather than stock dimensions.

scope_items.name: Wall openings and structure
scope_items.desc: Load calculations, engineered beams, and permits for opening the wall between a closed 1920s kitchen and the rooms people actually use.

scope_items.name: Ranges, ovens, and gas lines
scope_items.desc: Moving ranges, ovens, and refrigeration where the layout wants them, with new gas lines, venting, and dedicated circuits permitted and inspected.

scope_items.name: Lighting and electrical upgrades
scope_items.desc: Layered lighting design, plus the panel and service upgrades many older Gables homes need before an induction range or wine room shows up.

faqs.q: Do I need a permit to remodel a kitchen in Coral Gables?
faqs.a: If the project touches plumbing, gas, electrical, or structure, and a real kitchen remodel touches all four, then yes: permits through the city's Development Services Department, with inspections along the way. Swapping appliances into existing hookups or repainting does not need one. Unpermitted work has a way of surfacing during a sale in the Gables, and retroactive permitting costs more than doing it right once.

faqs.q: Will the Board of Architects need to see my kitchen plans?
faqs.a: Not for a purely interior remodel; that goes straight to plan review. The Board gets involved when your kitchen scope changes the exterior, like a larger window over the sink, a new vent through the facade, or a door out to the terrace. If your home is a designated historic property, exterior changes also need a Certificate of Appropriateness. We flag which path applies during the first walk-through.

faqs.q: How long will a custom kitchen remodel take?
faqs.a: Custom cabinetry is the honest schedule driver: quality cabinet packages take months to fabricate, which is why we order them early and sequence demolition so your house is not torn open while you wait. On-site construction typically runs a couple of months for a full kitchen, longer when structural openings are involved. Plan in seasons rather than weekends and you will not be disappointed.

faqs.q: Can you make a new kitchen fit a 1920s Mediterranean home?
faqs.a: That is most of what we do here. Arched openings can be echoed rather than fought, cabinet faces can be detailed to sit comfortably beside original millwork, and modern appliances can disappear behind panels. The trick is respecting scale and proportion, because a 1926 house will forgive a modern kitchen but not a warehouse-sized one. Good design plus careful carpentry keeps the room feeling inevitable.

faqs.q: What does a high-end kitchen remodel cost in Coral Gables?
faqs.a: Custom cabinetry and natural stone lead every kitchen budget, with appliances close behind, so the range is wide and driven by your selections. We would rather scope precisely than quote vaguely: after a walk-through you get a fixed written number tied to a specification, not an estimate that inflates mid-project. If the deciding factor is the lowest number, we will say so early and part on good terms.

kitchen-remodeling.cta_sub: Schedule a walk-through and get a fixed-scope written estimate for the kitchen, in English o en español, whichever language you cook in.

bathroom-remodeling.title: Bathroom Remodels for Coral Gables, FL Homes | PGX Builders
bathroom-remodeling.meta_description: Bathroom remodeling in Coral Gables — primary suites, frameless glass, flood-tested waterproofing in Miami's older homes. Estimates: (786) 273-2524.
bathroom-remodeling.h1: Primary baths, engineered behind the marble
bathroom-remodeling.hero_sub: Primary-suite and guest bath remodels across Coral Gables — frameless glass, stone, freestanding tubs, and waterproofing done to spec — fully permitted, inspected, and supervised daily by a licensed general contractor.
bathroom-remodeling.local_heading: Old Gables plumbing meets new Gables marble
intro_paragraphs: Bathrooms are where Coral Gables homes show their age first. Merrick-era houses near the Biltmore came with one modest bath per floor, and even the mid-century homes out in Gables by the Sea and Snapper Creek Lakes predate the idea of a primary suite with a double vanity, a freestanding tub, and a shower you can stand in without negotiating. So owners here remodel: combining a small bedroom and a hall bath into a real suite, or taking a dated eighties renovation down to the studs and doing it properly in stone.

Bathroom remodeling in Coral Gables is permitted through the city's Development Services Department, with plumbing, electrical, and mechanical inspections along the way. Purely interior work skips the Board of Architects; add or enlarge a window for natural light and the Board weighs in before the Building Division does. The bigger local issue is what sits behind the walls: original cast iron drains, galvanized supply lines, and slabs poured decades before anyone dreamed of a curbless shower. We scope those realities up front, because discovering them mid-demolition is how other people's projects lose their schedules.

PGX treats a bathroom as a small building with unforgiving tolerances. Waterproofing membranes get flood-tested before a single tile goes down, slopes get checked with a level rather than optimism, and stone is handled by installers who have earned the right to touch it. You get a fixed written scope, daily supervision, and protection for every finished surface between the front door and the work zone. Licensed and insured, Lic. CGC1539072, every project permitted and inspected, because a beautiful bathroom that leaks is just an expensive one.
bathroom-remodeling.scope_heading: What a Gables bath remodel covers
bathroom-remodeling.scope_intro: From powder rooms to full primary suites, the scope is settled in writing before the tile is ordered. The usual elements below.

scope_items.name: Bedroom and hall bath, combined
scope_items.desc: Reworking bedrooms, closets, and hall baths into a true suite, with layout, plumbing rough-ins, and permits handled as one package.

scope_items.name: Showers the slab can take
scope_items.desc: Curbless or low-curb entries where the slab allows, flood-tested pans, linear drains, and heavy glass hung on solid blocking rather than hope.

scope_items.name: Tubs the floor can hold
scope_items.desc: Tub placement with floor structure verified, plus marble and quartzite surfaces sealed and installed to survive daily use in Miami humidity.

scope_items.name: Full plumbing replacement
scope_items.desc: Swapping original cast iron and galvanized lines for modern drains and supply while the walls are open, the cheapest moment you will ever do it.

scope_items.name: Quiet exhaust, layered light
scope_items.desc: Quiet exhaust routed properly to the exterior, moisture-rated fixtures, and lighting layered for actual grooming instead of a single ceiling glare.

faqs.q: Do I need a permit for a bathroom remodel in Coral Gables?
faqs.a: Yes, for anything beyond cosmetics. Moving or replacing plumbing, altering electrical, or changing ventilation all require permits through Coral Gables Development Services, with inspections before things get closed up. That inspection sequence is your friend: it means the waterproofing and rough plumbing were verified before tile hid them. We pull the permits, schedule the inspections, and keep the paper trail you will want at resale.

faqs.q: My house still has original cast iron drains. Should we replace them now?
faqs.a: If the walls and floors are open anyway, almost always yes. Cast iron from the 1920s through the 1950s is at or past the end of its service life, and a beautiful new bathroom draining into a failing stack is a bad bet. We scope camera inspections early so you decide with facts, and replacement happens while access is free instead of after the marble is down.

faqs.q: Can I have a curbless shower in an older Coral Gables home?
faqs.a: Often, but it depends on the structure. On a slab, recessing the pan takes careful cutting and sometimes rerouted plumbing; on wood-framed second floors, we adjust framing to sink the pan. When the structure genuinely will not cooperate, a low-profile curb with a properly sloped pan is the honest alternative. We will tell you which one your floor supports before you fall in love with a photo.

faqs.q: Does the Board of Architects care about my bathroom?
faqs.a: Only when it shows from outside. An interior bath remodel goes through plan review without Board involvement; enlarging or adding a window, or venting through a visible facade, brings the Board in first. On designated historic homes, exterior changes need a Certificate of Appropriateness as well. Most bathroom scopes stay interior, so most of our Gables bath projects skip design review entirely, and we confirm which case is yours at the walk-through.

faqs.q: What does a primary bath remodel cost at this level?
faqs.a: Stone, glass, and plumbing fixtures set the tone, and the behind-the-wall work of new drains, supply, and ventilation is the part people underestimate. Rather than quote a fantasy range, we walk the space, scope what the building actually needs, and give you a fixed written number. As a high-end contractor we compete on certainty and finish quality, not on being the lowest of three bids.

bathroom-remodeling.cta_sub: Tell us what you want fixed and we will put a real scope and a real number on it, in English o en español.

home-additions.title: Coral Gables FL Home Additions | PGX Builders Group
home-additions.meta_description: Home additions in Coral Gables, FL — rear extensions, second stories, in-law suites. We handle Board of Architects review and permits. (786) 273-2524.
home-additions.hero_sub: Rear extensions, second stories, and garage conversions in Coral Gables — engineered, Board of Architects approved, permitted through Development Services, and built under the daily supervision of a licensed general contractor.
home-additions.local_heading: Additions that look like they were always there
intro_paragraphs: Coral Gables lots tend to be generous, and the smart money here builds on them rather than moving. The classic projects: a rear family room and primary suite behind a Mediterranean in the Country Club Section, a second story over a postwar ranch north of Bird Road, an in-law suite for a multigenerational household in Hammock Oaks. Estate owners in Old Cutler Bay and Journey's End add wings, not rooms. The common thread is that a home addition has to read as original, because this is not a city that forgives a bolted-on box.

Additions are precisely what the Coral Gables Board of Architects exists to review. Massing, rooflines, materials, and how the new volume sits beside the old one are all evaluated against the city's design standards before Development Services opens the building permit. Expect structural engineering for foundations and tie-beams, Miami-Dade approved products for new openings, and the city's tree protections if a specimen oak stands where your footprint wants to go. On waterfront streets in Gables by the Sea or Cocoplum, FEMA substantial-improvement rules can also shape how much you invest in the existing structure. We map all of it before you commit to drawings.

PGX has spent more than two decades building in South Florida, and additions are where that experience shows: tying new foundations to old ones, matching stucco textures and barrel tile so the seam disappears, and keeping the occupied half of the house livable while the new half goes up. The scope is fixed in writing before we start, a supervisor runs the site daily, and one accountable team carries the project from the first sketch through final inspection and warranty.
home-additions.scope_intro: Every addition starts with engineering and a clear picture of the design review it will face. These are the five we build most.

scope_items.name: Rear wings and family rooms
scope_items.desc: Family rooms, dens, and primary suites extended into the yard, with foundations, tie-beams, and roof tie-ins engineered and permitted as one package.

scope_items.name: Second floors, engineered first
scope_items.desc: Structural evaluation of the existing masonry and footings first, then a full upper floor designed to satisfy both the engineer and the Board of Architects.

scope_items.name: Garages and loggias, made livable
scope_items.desc: Turning underused covered space into conditioned rooms with insulation, impact openings, and mechanical extensions done legally, so the square footage counts when you sell.

scope_items.name: Suites for multigenerational households
scope_items.desc: Independent suites with baths and kitchenettes for long-stay family, built to code and scaled to the architecture rather than stapled onto it.

scope_items.name: Footings, steel, and tie-beams
scope_items.desc: Underpinning, new footings, steel, and tie-beam upgrades: the invisible half of an addition budget, and the half that determines whether it lasts.

faqs.q: Does every Coral Gables addition go through the Board of Architects?
faqs.a: Yes. Additions and new construction are core Board of Architects territory, reviewed against the city's design standards before the Building Division takes over for code review. The Board looks at massing, materials, rooflines, and how the addition relates to your house and the street. Designs that respect the original architecture tend to move through cleanly; designs that fight it invite revisions. We design for approval from the first sketch.

faqs.q: How long does a home addition take from idea to move-in?
faqs.a: Budget real time for the front end: design, structural engineering, Board of Architects review, and permitting commonly take months before ground breaks, and construction runs several more depending on size and whether a second story is involved. A year from first meeting to finished room is a realistic frame for substantial additions. We put the full timeline in writing so the process has no mystery phases.

faqs.q: Do FEMA flood rules limit what I can build on a waterfront lot?
faqs.a: They can shape the project. On flood-zone properties, including parts of Gables by the Sea, Cocoplum, and other bayfront streets, federal substantial-improvement rules compare your investment against the value of the existing structure; cross the threshold and the whole building must be brought into flood compliance. That is not automatically bad news, but it must be understood before design, not discovered at permitting. We run that analysis early.

faqs.q: Can my 1920s house structurally support a second story?
faqs.a: Many can, some need help, and a structural engineer settles it rather than a hunch. Original masonry walls and footings are evaluated first; reinforcement, new columns, or upgraded tie-beams are designed where required. Occasionally the honest answer is that a rear extension serves you better than going up. We coordinate the engineering and give you options with real numbers attached instead of a single take-it-or-leave-it plan.

faqs.q: Is adding on smarter than buying a bigger house in the Gables?
faqs.a: Frequently, if you love your street. An addition lets you keep the location, the canopy, and the tax base you have built up while buying exactly the space you are missing, and Gables lots often have room to grow. It is still major construction with design review and months of work, so it rewards owners planning to stay. We will give you a candid feasibility read before you spend on drawings.

home-additions.cta_sub: Show us the lot and the idea. We will talk feasibility, design review, and honest numbers, in English o en español.

outdoor-living.h1: Outdoor rooms for the City Beautiful
outdoor-living.hero_sub: Summer kitchens, pergolas, terraces, and driveways for Coral Gables homes — designed to pass the Board of Architects, permitted through the city, and built by a licensed, insured general contractor.
outdoor-living.local_heading: Outdoor living is the original Gables amenity
intro_paragraphs: George Merrick's architects understood the Miami evening, which is why courtyards, loggias, and arcades were built into Coral Gables homes from the start. The modern version of outdoor living is more ambitious: a summer kitchen and covered terrace behind a Riviera home, a pergola and fire feature in Snapper Creek Lakes, a pool terrace at Tahiti Beach that has to shrug off salt air from the bay. Owners here are not buying a grill on a slab. They are building an outdoor room that belongs to the architecture.

Exterior work is exactly what Coral Gables reviews most carefully. Terraces, pergolas, fences, and yes, driveways go before the Board of Architects, and Development Services permits the construction behind them. The city's tree rules mean a specimen oak near your project is a design constraint rather than something to clear away; removing protected trees, or even pruning them heavily, requires its own permit. Waterfront lots add flood-zone considerations for new structures. It sounds like a lot because it is a lot, and it is also why Gables streets look the way they do. We handle the approvals as part of the job, not as your homework.

PGX builds exterior work to interior standards. Gas, water, and electrical runs for summer kitchens are permitted and inspected; pergola footings are engineered rather than guessed; drainage is planned so the terrace sheds water away from the house instead of toward it. Projects run under a fixed written scope with daily supervision, and our crews know how to work behind the gates of Cocoplum or Gables Estates, where quiet, tidy job sites are the price of admission. Licensed and insured under Lic. CGC1539072, with 20-plus years of South Florida construction behind every estimate.

scope_items.desc: Outdoor kitchens with real utilities, meaning permitted gas, water, and electrical, plus counters and cabinetry rated for weather instead of just priced like it.

scope_items.name: Loggias and pergolas, engineered
scope_items.desc: Loggias, trellises, and shade structures with engineered footings and connections detailed for hurricane wind loads, matched to the lines of the house.

scope_items.name: Driveways the Board reviews too
scope_items.desc: Pavers, finished concrete, and walkways designed to satisfy the Board of Architects and drain properly through a Miami rainy season.

scope_items.name: Stucco, paint, and facades
scope_items.desc: Exterior restoration with stucco repair and color changes handled correctly, since in Coral Gables even the paint palette is a reviewed decision.

scope_items.name: Impact openings
scope_items.desc: Replacing terrace doors and exterior openings with Miami-Dade approved impact units that protect the house without cheapening the elevation.

faqs.q: Do I need permits for a summer kitchen or pergola in Coral Gables?
faqs.a: Yes on both counts. Structures need building permits, the gas, electrical, and plumbing runs need their own trade permits, and because it is all exterior, the Board of Architects reviews the design first. It is more process than a grill island seems to deserve, but it is the same process that keeps Gables backyards looking like the Gables. We manage the approvals as part of the project.

faqs.q: There is a big oak where I want the terrace. Can it come down?
faqs.a: Not without a city permit, and if it qualifies as a specimen tree, generally 18 inches in trunk diameter or more, removal triggers mitigation requirements. Coral Gables protects its canopy seriously, and the fastest path is usually designing with the tree instead of against it: shifting the footprint, floating a deck over the roots, shaping shade into the plan. We have done both and will tell you which fight is worth having.

faqs.q: Will salt air near the bay wreck my outdoor kitchen?
faqs.a: It will wreck the wrong materials. Along Gables by the Sea, Cocoplum, and other bayfront streets we specify marine-grade stainless, coated or naturally inert metals, dense stone sealed properly, and hardware chosen for coastal exposure. Cheap outdoor cabinets and big-box fixtures corrode fast in that environment. Specify once, correctly, and the terrace ages like the house instead of like a rental grill.

faqs.q: How disruptive is a backyard project to daily life?
faqs.a: Less than interior work, but not invisible: expect material staging, concrete days, and a stretch when the yard belongs to the crew. We plan access routes to protect landscaping and hardscape, keep the site clean daily, and follow the conduct and hours rules that gated communities along Old Cutler Road enforce. Most clients live normally throughout, minus the backyard itself.

faqs.q: What should I expect to invest in a full outdoor living project?
faqs.a: It scales with utilities and structure: a paver terrace is one budget, while a covered outdoor room with a full summer kitchen, gas, water, and electrical is genuinely another. Selections like appliances, stone, and cabinetry move the number as much as square footage does. We scope it in writing after a site walk so you are comparing real specifications, not a per-foot guess that ignores what is under the slab.

outdoor-living.cta_sub: Walk us through the yard and the vision, and a fixed written scope comes back, in English o en español.

permitting-compliance.local_heading: How work gets approved in the Gables
intro_paragraphs: Most people do not go looking for a permitting contractor until something forces the issue. A title search on a Riviera bungalow turns up a 1990s addition permit nobody ever closed. A refinance on a Cocoplum waterfront house stalls because the generator and the pool heater were never inspected. A buyer's inspector notices that the enclosed Florida room on a Country Club Section home appears nowhere in the city's records. Coral Gables housing stock is old enough, and trades hands often enough, that this happens constantly, and it always surfaces at the least convenient hour.

Work here is filed electronically with the City of Coral Gables Development Services Department and reviewed by its Building Division. Anything visible from the street, from windows and doors to roofs, driveways and even exterior paint colors, goes to the Board of Architects first, and designated historic properties need a Certificate of Appropriateness before permits move. Windows, doors and roofing systems require Miami-Dade product approvals for the High-Velocity Hurricane Zone, installed exactly as the approval reads. On the water in Gables Estates, Tahiti Beach or Deering Bay, the city's floodplain administrator also weighs whether a project counts as substantial improvement.

Compliance work rewards contractors who read the file before they promise anything, and PGX has been reading South Florida files for over 20 years, across more than 150 remodels and additions, all of them permitted and inspected. We coordinate the engineer or architect a record requires instead of pretending to be one, we open up what needs to be seen before we scope it, and one supervisor calls the inspections and is standing there when they happen. Nobody here will tell you a shortcut exists, because in the Gables it does not.
permitting-compliance.scope_heading: The compliance work we take on

scope_items.desc: Pulling the full permit history, establishing what was actually built, then filing, correcting or re-inspecting whatever each one needs before it can be closed.

scope_items.name: Applications the Gables accepts

faqs.q: There is an open permit on my Coral Gables house and I am trying to sell. What now?
faqs.a: Get the actual record rather than the one-line summary the title company sent. The city's permit portal shows what was filed, what was inspected and exactly where it stopped. From there it is usually one of three things: a missing final inspection, work built beyond what was approved, or a permit whose contractor is long gone. Each has a path, none of them is instant, so start the day you hear about it rather than the week of closing.

faqs.q: Can you close out a permit that another contractor pulled?
faqs.a: Usually yes. A permit tied to a contractor who has disappeared, or one that has expired, generally has to be revived or re-filed under a licensed contractor willing to stand behind the work. That means we look at what is actually there first. If the construction is sound, it gets inspected and closed. If it is not, you get an honest scope for making it right. We do not put our license on work we have not opened up.

faqs.q: Does the Board of Architects get involved in a permit cleanup?
faqs.a: The moment the work shows from outside, yes. Coral Gables routes exterior changes to the Board of Architects before the Building Division finishes its review, and that reaches things owners rarely expect, including exterior paint. If what you are legalizing is an unpermitted window swap or a patio enclosure, design review is part of the path rather than a formality bolted on at the end. We assemble submittals in that order so it happens once.

faqs.q: Our condo board received a recertification notice. Is that work PGX does?
faqs.a: The report itself comes from a Florida-licensed engineer or architect, and we coordinate that professional rather than pretend to be one. What PGX does is the work the report calls for: concrete restoration, structural repairs, electrical upgrades, railings and parking-lot items, permitted and inspected through the same Development Services process. Coral Gables mails Notices of Required Recertification to buildings that reach the age the county code sets, and repeats it on a fixed cycle after that. Milestone inspections and reserve studies run on their own track for condominium and cooperative buildings.

faqs.q: How much does it cost to legalize unpermitted work in Coral Gables?
faqs.a: Entirely dependent on what is behind the wall. A missing final inspection on sound construction is a small item. A room addition built without engineering, or a re-roof done without approved products, can mean opening things up and rebuilding them to code. We will not quote a number before we look, and we will not hand you a low one to win the job and revise it later. You get a written scope, real allowances, and the bad news early.
